headline: Highest risk is data leakage: cognee handles personal/finance data while awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable docs list with no shared channel, so other risks stay limited.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable and exposes no I/O surfaces, while cognee’s documented surfaces are API/CLI oriented with tenant isolation. No shared channel, filesystem bridge, or parser path is documented, so a prompt-injection pathway between them is not evidenced.
conditions: IF a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge is added between the pair, injection risk becomes plausible.
IF either agent begins parsing the other’s raw text as instructions, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not copy raw outputs between them.
Disable any shared clipboard or message queue.
Review any future MCP or filesystem bridge before enabling it.

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee touches personal data, finance data, and support history, but awesome-selfhosted is a docs-only knowledge-management list with no runtime I/O. The pair lacks a documented shared workspace or upload path, so leakage is possible only if an operator manually moves sensitive content into the docs workflow.
conditions: IF sensitive customer data is manually pasted into awesome-selfhosted-related notes, leakage risk increases.
IF a shared filesystem or synced workspace is introduced, reassess upward.
mitigations: Avoid placing customer data in shared notes.
Use separate folders for each agent.
Redact personal and finance data before transfer.
Restrict API keys to cognee only.
Audit any future sync or export path.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is not runnable and has no write or network permissions, while cognee uses CLI tooling with session-scoped memory and allowlisted egress. There is no overlapping mutable resource or shared write surface documented, so direct capability conflict is not plausible.
conditions: IF awesome-selfhosted is turned into a writable runtime component, reassess conflict risk.
IF both agents are given write access to the same directory or database, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep awesome-selfhosted read-only.
Do not grant shared write access.
Separate any databases or caches.
Use per-agent credentials.
Document ownership of mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: cognee can store and reuse workflows, decisions, and successful implementations, so it may treat upstream content as reusable context. However, awesome-selfhosted is a static list rather than an action-taking agent, so the cascade is limited to misclassification or bad retrieval, not autonomous downstream execution.
conditions: IF cognee is configured to ingest awesome-selfhosted content as authoritative knowledge, cascade risk increases.
IF downstream automation is attached to cognee outputs, reassess upward.
mitigations: Mark imported content as untrusted.
Add a verification step before reuse.
Limit ingestion to curated sources.
Separate reference data from operational workflows.
Review any automation triggered by retrieved facts.

E_compliance.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while awesome-selfhosted is a public docs/listing project with no stated retention or residency controls. The mismatch is not a direct violation by itself, but if regulated data is routed through the pair, the lack of documented compliance controls on the docs side creates a default-policy gap.
conditions: IF regulated personal or finance data is stored in cognee and mirrored into shared docs, compliance risk increases.
IF a residency or retention policy is required for the workflow, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of public docs.
Add a retention policy for shared notes.
Tag sensitive records before ingestion.
Review residency requirements before use.
Use access controls on any exported artifacts.
